body:
Correcting my own BUG-1286 diagnosis before an implementer builds the wrong half — plus a fingerprint that makes BUG-1290 step 1 a lookup

Both of these are comments on the specs, and comments do not bind an implementer. BUG-1286 is Approved high and queued, so if you agree, the first one needs to move into acceptance rather than sit under it.

BUG-1286: I GOT THE DIAGNOSIS PARTLY WRONG. BUG-1234 shipped end to end at 21:48 today and I read its full stream. PrMerged IS emitted, and it IS keyed to the spec:

  21:47:58  PhaseEntered idx=4 merge
  21:48:01  PrMerged pr=1975
  21:48:01  PhaseEntered idx=5 pull
  21:48:11  PhaseEntered idx=6 build
  21:50:41  PhaseDonePr pr=1975

So the drain path is not missing a terminal event. PhaseDonePr fires two minutes forty after the merge and overwrites it as the spec's last word. That is what the 219 PhaseDonePr endings actually are — not failures to emit, but successful merges whose terminal event was buried by a later phase event. Your 206 UnshippedWorkDetected endings are the same shape.

Which makes this two defects needing different fixes, and the acceptance as filed covers only the second:

  1. ORDERING, affecting every drain-driven spec. A terminal event must be the LAST event for that spec. Either the trailing phases stop emitting spec-keyed events after PrMerged, or a completion event is emitted at the end of the run once pull and build finish. I lean to the second — pull and build genuinely happen and suppressing them loses information — but it is your call.
  2. MISSING EMISSION, affecting specs closed outside a drain run: batch trailers and the pull auto-bump. This is the half I got right, and TASK-1285 and BUG-1207 are its examples.

Fixing only 2 leaves every successful drain still ending on PhaseDonePr, which is the majority case. The success condition worth writing into the spec: a consumer can take the last event for a spec and correctly decide whether it is finished, without joining against the store. Today that fails in both directions.

The live case also settles your no-backfill guard favourably — this is current behaviour on today's binary, not a dated artifact.

BUG-1290: FINGERPRINT. In all 292 spurious back-to-back pairs, the SECOND event has no `seat` field. 292 of 292. The first carries one 172 times. Since seat is Option<String> with skip_serializing_if on events.rs:70, the spurious emitter is simply the one passing None. BUG-1234's pair shows it cleanly: 21:35:36 reviewer with seat=reviewer, 21:35:48 reviewer without.

That turns "name the two call sites" into a lookup. I put an explicit caution in the comment: absence of seat is a fingerprint for LOCATING the emitter, not a runtime filter — 120 first-of-pair events also lack it, because seat is legitimately unknown for phase 1. "Drop PhaseEntered with no seat" would be a second wrong fix in the same spec.

Neither changes your reframing; both make the first implementation step cheaper.

Wave: BUG-1234 Completed via #1975 with no rework round, BUG-1231 now in phase 1, sixteen queued behind it.
